title: Maravillosos et piadosos
subtitle: Cantiga de Santa María no. 139
stanzas: Santa Maria, a que nos guia
does Holy Mary work, who guides us
ben noit' e dia et nos dá paz.
well by night and day and gives us peace.
E dest' un miragre vos contar quero
And of these I wish to tell you a miracle
que en Frandes aquesta Virgen fez,
that this Virgin worked in Flanders,
Madre de Deus, maravillos' et fero
Mother of God, wondrous and mighty,
por unha dona que foi unha vez.
for a lady who once went
A sa eigreja desta que seja
to her church: may she be
por nós, et vejamola sa faz
for us, and may we see her face
no Parayso, u Deus dar quiso
in Paradise, where God willed to give
goyo et riso a quen lle praz.
joy and laughter to those who please Him.
This lady took a little boy,
seu fillo, sigo, que en offrecon
her son, with her, whom as an offering
she had given to the Virgin when very small,
que de mal ll' o guardass' e d'o queijon.
that she might keep him from harm and grief,
Et lle fezesse per que disesse
and make him such that he would always say
sempr' e soubesse den ben assaz,
and know a great deal of good;
que, com' aprendo, seu pan comendo foi.
and, as I learn, he went along eating his bread.
Running, he stopped before the image.
Beside the Son of that image
the little boy said: “Will you eat?”
Mais la figura da Virgen mui sagen
But the figure of the Virgin, most wise,
diss' a seu Fillo: “Dille sen tardar
said to her Son: “Tell him without delay
que non ss'espante, mais tigo jante
not to be afraid, but to dine with you
where he may ever sing and have solace,
e seja quito do mui maldito
and be free of the most accursed
devil, who is written down as wicked.”
Quand' esto diss', a omagen de Christo
When she had said this, the image of Christ
cras mig' en Ceo; e pois que me visto
with me tomorrow in Heaven; and since you have seen me,
you shall be with me for evermore.
U ouças quanto cada un santo canta,
There you will hear all that each saint sings,
So it came to pass: the boy passed away
e moço e ido a Deus vi’az.

title: El Fuego
subtitle: Ensalada
stanzas: No os tardéis en traer luego
Do not delay in bringing at once
water to the fire, water to the fire!
Este fuego que se enciende es el maldito pecado,
This fire being kindled is accursed sin,
que al que no halla ocupado siempre para sí lo prende.
which seizes for itself whoever it finds idle.
Cualquier que de Dios pretende salvación procure luego
Whoever seeks salvation from God, let him bring at once
agua al fuego, agua al fuego.
water to the fire, water to the fire.
Venid presto, pecadores, a matar aqueste fuego;
Come quickly, sinners, and put out this fire;
haced penitencia luego de todos vuestros errores.
do penance at once for all your errors.
Reclamen esas campanas dentro en vuestros corazones.
Let those bells ring out within your hearts.
Poned en Dios las aficiones, todas las gentes humanas.
Set your affections on God, all humankind.
¡Llamad esos aguadores, luego, luego, sin tardar!
Call the water-carriers, quickly, quickly, without delay!
Y ayúdennos a matar este fuego.
And help us put out this fire.
No os tardéis en traer luego dentro de vuestra conciencia
Do not delay in bringing at once into your conscience
mil cargos de penitencia de buen agua,
a thousand loads of penance of good water,
y ansí mataréis la fragua de vuestros malos deseos,
and so you will quench the forge of your evil desires,
and the foul enemies will flee.
Oh, how the world is burning,
con lo que el demonio amasa!
Por cualquiera que traspasa los mandamientos de Dios,
For whoever breaks the commandments of God
thou shalt cast them into the fire;
in miseries they shall not stand.”
Este mundo donde andamos es una herviente fragua,
This world in which we walk is a seething forge,
donde no ha lugar el agua, si por ventura tardamos.
where water is of no avail if by chance we are late.
¡Oh, cómo nos abrasamos en el mundo y su hervor!
Oh, how we burn in the world and its heat!
Por cualquiera pecador que lo que da Dios no toma,
Of any sinner who will not take what God gives
se dirá lo que de Roma cuando se ardía sin favor:
it shall be said what was said of Rome as it burned, helpless:
“Mira Nero, de Tarpeya, a Roma cómo se ardía;
“From the Tarpeian Rock Nero watched how Rome was burning;
gritos dan niños y viejos y él de nada se dolía”.
children and old men cried out, and he grieved for nothing.”
Do not delay! Bring, bring water now!
And you, cut it off! Run! Help, quickly!
en dar golpes a los pechos!
Run, run! Quickly cut those beams!
Y ansí, con justa razón dirán las gentes humanas:
And so, with good reason, all humankind will say:
“¿dónde las hay las tales aguas soberanas?”
“Where are such sovereign waters to be found?”
Toca, Huan, con tu gaitilla, pues ha cesado el pesar.
Play, Juan, on your little bagpipe, for the sorrow has ceased.
Yo te diré un cantar muy pulido a maravilla.
I will sing you a song, wondrously fine.
Veslo aquí, ea pues, todos decir:
Here it is; come then, everyone say:
Y es que ha hecho criatura
For she has made a creature
of the eternal Son of God,
as we have come to know,
que nos vino en este día
for it came to us on this day
to the shepherd of the lambs.
que es de agua dulce y buena,
which is of sweet, good water,
so that it may be said of us:

title: Yo canto, yo lloro
subtitle: Salve in the vernacular
stanzas: But if I die of the love
as I sing of her purity
If I live, it is because I will it;
if I will it, it is a glory,
Y entre el placer y el llanto
desde el instante de tu concepción.
from the instant of your conception.
and let the beautiful stars proclaim it,
and the intelligences of higher light,
God save you, most pure Virgin,
desde el instante de tu concepción.
from the instant of your conception.

title: Ríu, ríu, chíu
subtitle: Christmas villancico
stanzas: Ríu, ríu, chíu, la guarda ribera,
Riu, riu, chiu, the keeper of the riverbank:
Dios guardó el lobo de nuestra cordera.
God kept the wolf from our lamb.
El lobo rabioso la quiso morder
The raging wolf tried to bite her,
Mas Dios poderoso la supo defender
but almighty God knew how to defend her;
Quísola hacer que no pudiese pecar
He willed to make her unable to sin,
Ni aun original esta virgen no tuviera.
so that this virgin had not even original sin.
Este que es nacido es el gran monarca
He who is born is the great monarch,
Christ the Patriarch, clothed in flesh;
Hanos redimido con se hacer chiquito
He has redeemed us by making himself small;
Aunque era infinito finito se hiciera.
though He was infinite, He became finite.
Yo vi mil garzones que andaban cantando
I saw a thousand youths going about singing,
Por aquí volando haciendo mil sones
flying around here, making a thousand sounds,
Diciendo a gascones “Gloria sea en el Cielo”
saying to the shepherds: “Glory be in Heaven,
Y paz en el suelo pues Jesús naciera.
and peace on earth, for Jesus is born.”
Pues que ya tenemos lo que deseamos
Since we now have what we longed for,
let us all go together and bring Him gifts;
we shall all give Him our good will,
Pues a se igualar con nosotros viniera.
since He came to make himself one of us.

title: Quedito airecillo
subtitle: Tono to the Nativity
stanzas: do not come, do not come,
for though he sleeps, he keeps watch.

title: Pues el cielo y la tierra
subtitle: Christmas villancico
stanzas: Pues el cielo y la tierra dicen las obras
Since heaven and earth proclaim the works
del que nace, y las puertas abre a la gloria.
of Him who is born, and the gates open to glory.
Heaven, tell Him, tell Him sweet words.
Sean de sus grandezas todos idiomas,
Let all tongues speak of His greatness,
pues el cielo y la tierra dicen sus obras.
for heaven and earth proclaim His works.
Aplauda la tierra la flor generosa,
Let the earth applaud the noble flower
que porque se salven de ruinas las otras,
who, so that the others may be saved from ruin,
El aire se goce de ver que coronan
Let the air rejoice to see angelic hosts
que cantando a Dios hombre la gala,
for, singing the praises of God made man,

title: Antorcha brillante
subtitle: Tono to the Nativity
stanzas: for if I behold your light
hoy nace el autor de la vida.
today the author of life is born.
Take care, vigils; take care, yearnings;
Tened temor, que anda el amor
Con tan divino impulso gloria le cantan,
With such divine impulse they sing Him glory
Que al ver Dios nacido se alegra la noche santa.
that, seeing God born, the holy night rejoices.
Oh, qué feliz mi pecho será, si alcanza a ver
Oh, how happy my heart will be if it may see
Al Rey del cielo que nos regala su Gracia.
the King of Heaven, who grants us His grace.

title: La Negrina
subtitle: Ensalada
stanzas: pues Dios se ha hecho mortal.
God’s will to be born today.
who do you think He must be?”
Pues que tan bien lo has chapado
Since you have hit it so well,
tell us who this one is.
He is the Word made flesh,
un cantar si Dios te deja:
a song, if God allows you:
Ah, she wants it pleated, Bernat,
No nos cansemos, con placer cantemos
Let us not tire; let us sing with pleasure,
pues Dios y hombre es ya nacido.
for God and man is now born.
What will that lost Lucifer do,
pues que le quitó su ser
now that his power was taken from him
by the Virgin, mother and spouse?
que o vento le volvía la folha”.
and the wind turned its petals.”
Let us walk on and we shall see
What shall we say, what shall we sing
al que nos libró de mal,
to Him who freed us from evil,
y al alma de ser cativa?
God keep you, Señor Juan Branca,
Do you know that there has been born,
Sa muy ben, sa muy ben.
I know it well, I know it well.
Let’s go and see his birth;
God lies laid in a manger.
Hey! Come and you will see.
He is beautiful, he is beautiful;

title: Vaya, pues, rompiendo el aire
subtitle: Solo jácara, very lively
stanzas: So let it go, cleaving the air,
born, as it is, for the night
a la noche por lo guapo,
a la salud del Rey niño
to the health of the Child King
who lies shivering in the frost.
ay, Jesús, que de risa me caigo
ah, Jesus, I’m falling over with laughter,
y hasta el sol está tiritando.
and even the sun is shivering.
Here goes a jácara of the bold,
who will set the world on fire
the day that he grows angry,
the one who makes us believe
que hoy es el día que nace,
that today is the day he is born,
when we know that he is
El que siendo, allá en su patria,
He who, there in his homeland,
dormir le hace en un pesebre
is made to sleep in a manger
by a fickle woman’s sweet tooth,
tan guapo que el mismo día
so bold that on the very day
en que le parió su madre

title: Canten dos pajarillos
subtitle: Duo to the Nativity
stanzas: Canten dos pajarillos al tierno infante,
Let two little birds sing to the tender infant,
porque dos pajaritos al niño acallen,
so that two little birds may hush the child;
canten suaves, que esta noche del cielo sus voces salen.
let them sing softly, for tonight their voices come from heaven.
A esta noche la llaman la noche-buena,
This night they call the Good Night,
para todos de gozo, de gusto, de gloria, y a Dios de pena.
for all a night of joy, delight and glory, and for God of pain.
Porque sepan que, amante, dio cuanto tuvo:
So that they may know that, loving, He gave all He had,
este niño amoroso, donoso, gracioso, viene desnudo.
this loving child, so graceful, so charming, comes naked.
Hoy el niño de perlas llora entre pajas,
Today the child of pearls weeps among the straw,
y las aves cantando, saltando, volando le hacen la salva.
and the birds, singing, leaping, flying, give him their salute.

title: La Bomba
subtitle: Ensalada
stanzas: vayan los cargos al mar, que nos imos a anegar,
Cargo overboard, for we are sinking,
and no remedy can be hoped for.
Al escota socorred, vosotros id al timón,
Help at the sheet! You, go to the helm!
How slow! Run, run! Do you not see our ruin?
Esas gúmenas cortad porque se amaine la vela,
Cut those cables so the sail may be lowered;
hacia acá contrapesad, oh, que la nave se asuela,
counterweight this way, oh, the ship is going down!
mandad calafetear que quizá dará remedio,
Have it caulked, perhaps that will save us;
ya no hay tiempo ni lugar, que la nao se abre por medio,
there is no time or place left, the ship is splitting in two.
What shall we do? Will it help to swim?
Oh, que está tan bravo el mar, que todos pereceremos.
Oh, the sea is so wild that we shall all perish.
Santa Virgen de Loreto, San Ginés, socorrednos,
Holy Virgin of Loreto, Saint Genesius, help us,
que me ahogo, santo Dios, San Telmo, santo bendito,
for I am drowning, holy God, Saint Elmo, blessed saint;
oh Virgen de Guadalupe, nuestra maldad no te ocupe,
oh Virgin of Guadalupe, let our wickedness not trouble you;
Señora de Montserrate, oíd, señora y gran rescate.
Lady of Montserrat, hear us, Lady and great ransom.
Oh gran socorro y bonanza, nave viene en que escapemos,
Oh, great help and calm! Here comes a ship in which we may escape;
allegad, que perecemos, socorred, no haya tardanza.
come closer, for we are perishing; help, let there be no delay.
¿No sea un punto detenido?, señores, ¡ese batel, ese batel!
Let it not stop a moment! Gentlemen, that boat, that boat!
Oh, qué ventura he tenido, pues que pude entrar en él.
Oh, what good fortune I have had, for I managed to get into it.
“Gratias agamus, Domino, Deo nostro, dignum et justum est.”
“Let us give thanks to the Lord our God: it is right and just.”
De tan grande beneficio, recibido en este día,
For so great a blessing received this day,
cantemos con alegría, Todos hoy por su servicio.
let us sing with joy, all of us today in His service.
Ea, ea, sus, ¡empecemos! Empieza tú, Gil Pizarra,
Come on, come on, up, let us begin! You start, Gil Pizarra,
A tañer con tu guitarra, Y nosotros te ayudaremos.
playing your guitar, and we will help you.
Esperad que esté templada, ¡tiémplala bien, hi de ruin!
Wait until it is tuned; tune it well, you rascal!
Oh, cómo está destemplada, acaba, maldito, ya.
Oh, how out of tune it is! Get on with it, confound you!
Es por demás, sube, sube un poco más. Muy bien está.
It’s no use; up, up a little more. Now it is just right.
Ande, pues, nuestro apellido, el tañer con el cantar,
So let our cry go forth, playing and singing,
concordes en alabar, a Jesús recién nacido.
in concord to praise the newborn Jesus.
Bendito el que ha venido, a librarnos de agonía,
Blessed is He who has come to free us from anguish;
bendito sea este día, que nació el contentamiento,
blessed be this day, on which contentment was born;
His coming has remedied a thousand sorrows.
Benditos sean los ojos, que con piedad nos miraron,
Blessed be the eyes that looked on us with pity,
y benditos, que así amansaron tal fortuna.
and blessed, for thus they calmed such a storm.
No quede congoja alguna, demos prisa al navegar,
Let no anguish remain; let us hasten our sailing,
Poys o vento nos ha de llevar, Garrido vendaval.
for the wind must carry us, a fine southerly gale.
No se vio bonanza igual sobre tan gran desatiento.
Never was such calm seen after so great a disaster.
Bien hayas tú, viento, que ansí me ayudas contra fortuna.
Blessings on you, wind, for thus you help me against the storm.
Gritad, gritad todos a una gritad,
Gala es todo a nadie hoy duela, la gala chinela,
All is festivity, let no one grieve today, the gala chinela,
de la china gala la gala chinela,
de la china gala la gala chinela;
we promise much in a fierce storm,
but then we offer endless candle wax,
de la china gala la gala chinela.
de la china gala la gala chinela.
